key_insight: Predicting future scenes is more efficient and scalable when models focus on sparse, interaction-driven point trajectories and simulate futures step-by-step, enabling broad exploration of plausible long-horizon outcomes with explicit uncertainty.
problem_solved: Reduces the computational and representational burden of dense video prediction by shifting to sparse trajectory-based prediction, allowing efficient, uncertainty-aware exploration of many plausible long-term futures.
method: Represent scenes as sparse sets of salient points and model their trajectories instead of predicting dense pixel appearance.
Simulate futures iteratively along interaction chains (stepwise rollouts) to capture long-range dynamics without compounding dense errors.
Incorporate uncertainty-aware sampling or probabilistic outputs to generate diverse hypothesis sets while remaining computationally efficient.
impact: Enables scalable long-horizon forecasting and richer hypothesis generation for applications like robotics, planning, and autonomous systems, improving decision-making under uncertainty while reducing compute and memory costs.
visual_elements: Side-by-side illustration: dense video prediction (heavy, pixel-wise) vs sparse point-trajectory prediction (lightweight, focused).
Flowchart of stepwise rollout: current state → predict next sparse trajectories → iterate to form long-horizon futures.
‘Fan’ visualization showing multiple plausible futures arising from uncertainty-aware sampling.
Bar/line chart comparing computation or memory cost vs prediction horizon and diversity (sparse approach vs dense baseline).
paper_title: Envisioning the Future, One Step at a Time
paper_authors: Stefan Andreas Baumann, Jannik Wiese, Tommaso Martorella, Mahdi M. Kalayeh, Björn Ommer
